name: Returns Coordinator (TIER-R complete)
_comment: Book §10.9. Deterministic workflow — the returns coordinator's copying, done right. Every TIER-R property is a node or setting here. Importable to n8n; swap credential/URL placeholders. See ch10/README.md.

parameters._comment: T — Triggered reliably: an email trigger (event, not polling). Monitor processed-volume elsewhere to catch a silent trigger death.
Deterministic parse: fixed-format notification, so a regex extracts order_id and tracking. NO AI needed — the flowchart draws itself.
I — Idempotent: claim a key (message_id + order_id) in a Postgres state table. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; if 0 rows affected, this was already processed — the IF node below stops.
parameters.query: INSERT INTO wf_processed(key) VALUES (concat($1::text,'|',$2::text)) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING key;

parameters._comment: Stop if already processed (claim returned no row).
Act THROUGH the governed Ch.9 order server, not a raw ERP credential. E — retry-with-backoff on transient failure (retryOnFail).
Write tracking to the returns system (idempotent upstream via the claim). retryOnFail on transient errors.
Send templated acknowledgment (safe: idempotency claim already prevents a duplicate send on retry).
parameters.subject: Your return is on its way

parameters._comment: R — Reportable: log the completed run + emit a processed metric. A DROP in this metric alerts to a silently dead trigger (the T failure error-monitoring misses).
parameters.jsCode:
console.log(JSON.stringify({event:'returns_processed', order_id:$json.order_id, at:new Date().toISOString()}));
return [{ json: { logged: true } }];

parameters._comment: E — dead-letter path: unparseable emails and hard failures route here for human review instead of crashing the run half-done. Also posts an alert.

settings._comment: E — errorWorkflow routes any uncaught node failure to the dead-letter workflow.
